slides.say: How many odd numbers are there between twenty and eighty?

slides: We need to count them without listing all of them. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, jumping by two from the first odd number to the last, and then taking half of all the numbers.

slides.say: [short pause] The math way first. Twenty and eighty are even, so they wouldn't count anyway. The first odd number after twenty is twenty-one, and the last odd number before eighty is seventy-nine.
at: The first odd number after twenty

slides.say: Odd numbers go up in steps of two. From twenty-one to seventy-nine is seventy-nine minus twenty-one, which is fifty-eight. Fifty-eight divided by two is twenty-nine. Careful, twenty-nine is the number of steps, the gaps between the odd numbers. It's not the number of odd numbers. That's choice number one, and it's a trap.
at: That's choice number one, and it's a trap

slides.say: Each step lands on a new odd number, and we also count the first one, twenty-one. So twenty-nine plus one is thirty. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way, by understanding. Count all the whole numbers from twenty-one to eighty, both ends included. Eighty is even, so adding it doesn't add an odd number. Eighty minus twenty-one, plus one, is sixty.

They take turns, odd, even, odd, even. The list starts with an odd number, twenty-one, and ends with an even number, eighty, so they come in pairs, and exactly half of them are odd. Sixty divided by two is thirty. Sixty, choice number four, forgets to take half. So choice number two is our answer again, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: So choice number two is our answer again
